questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: Match each hormone to its structure class — 1) T3/T4  2) Serotonin  3) Insulin  4) Aldosterone … A) Tryptophan derivative  B) Steroid hormone  C) Tyrosine derivative  D) Large peptide
questions.exp: Tyrosine derivatives are T3/T4 and catecholamines; serotonin and melatonin are tryptophan derivatives; insulin is a large peptide; aldosterone is a steroid. (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: All of the following are catecholamines of the adrenal medulla EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Catecholamines (adrenal medulla) are adrenaline (80%), noradrenaline and dopamine; melatonin is a tryptophan derivative. (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: Adrenaline forms what percentage of adrenal medulla catecholamines?
questions.exp: Adrenaline is 80% of the catecholamines of the adrenal medulla. (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: Growth hormone is a large peptide of ___ amino acids.
questions.exp: Growth hormone has 191 amino acids (prolactin 199, insulin 51). (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: Prolactin is a large peptide of ___ amino acids.
questions.exp: Prolactin has 199 amino acids (growth hormone 191, insulin 51). (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: The number of amino acids in insulin is:
questions.exp: Insulin has 51 amino acids and is grouped under large peptides (>50 AA). (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: Which of the following is classed as a SMALL peptide (<50 amino acids)?
questions.exp: Small peptides (<50 AA) include ACTH, ADH, oxytocin and all hypothalamic hormones; GH, prolactin, insulin, PTH and renin are large peptides. (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: ‘Glycoprotein hormones (FSH, LH, TSH) contain more carbohydrate than protein.’
questions.exp: Glycoproteins are defined as protein > carbohydrate; FSH/LH/TSH are >200 AA with a common α subunit. (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: FSH, LH and TSH share which structural feature?
opts: A common α subunit and >200 amino acids
A common β subunit and 51 amino acids
questions.exp: The glycoproteins FSH, LH and TSH are >200 AA and share a common α subunit. (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: Match the adrenal cortex zone to its hormone — 1) Zona glomerulosa  2) Zona fasciculata  3) Zona reticularis … A) Cortisol  B) Aldosterone  C) Androgens (DHEAS/androstenedione)
questions.exp: Zona glomerulosa → aldosterone; zona fasciculata → cortisol; zona reticularis → adrenal androgens (DHEAS, androstenedione). (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: DHEAS is described as the most abundant adreno-cortical hormone during:
questions.exp: Note: DHEAS (dihydroepiandrosterone sulfate) is the most abundant adreno-cortical hormone in fetal life. (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the sex hormones listed?
questions.exp: Sex hormones are estrogen, progesterone and testosterone; cortisol is an adrenal cortex (fasciculata) steroid. (Book p830)

questions.sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830
questions.q: The vitamin-derivative hormones listed are:
questions.exp: Vitamin derivatives in the classification are vitamin A and vitamin D. (Book p830)

questions.sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831
questions.q: The most abundant source of serotonin is:
questions.exp: Serotonin's most abundant source is the enterochromaffin cells of the GIT; melatonin's is the pineal gland. (Book p831)

questions.sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831
questions.q: The most abundant source of melatonin is:
questions.exp: Melatonin's most abundant source is the pineal gland. (Book p831)

questions.sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831
questions.q: ‘Serotonin and melatonin act as centrally-acting neurotransmitters and peripherally-acting hormones.’
questions.exp: Both are centrally acting neurotransmitters and peripherally acting hormones. (Book p831)

questions.sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831
questions.q: In the sleep–wake cycle, the transmitter that keeps us alert and active is:
questions.exp: Serotonin keeps us alert and active; melatonin helps in sleep. (Book p831)

questions.sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831
questions.q: At night (9:30–10 pm) light signals fall. What happens to serotonin and melatonin respectively?
questions.exp: At night, reduced light signals lower serotonin, allowing melatonin to rise (gradual, maximum at 2–2:30 am). (Book p831)

questions.sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831
questions.q: Melatonin levels reach their maximum at about:
questions.exp: Melatonin rises gradually at night with maximum levels at 2–2:30 am. (Book p831)

questions.sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831
questions.q: A teenager overuses gadgets at night. The downstream consequence that can ultimately result is:
opts: Depression, via disrupted serotonin and a sleep–wake cycle that cannot raise melatonin
questions.exp: Gadget overuse at night keeps serotonin up so melatonin cannot rise, disrupting the sleep–wake cycle and serotonin levels, which can lead to depression. (Book p831)

questions.sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831
questions.q: Match the ‘hormones of happiness’ (DOSE) — D  O  S  E … A) Oxytocin  B) Endorphins  C) Dopamine  D) Serotonin
questions.exp: DOSE = Dopamine, Oxytocin, Serotonin, Endorphins. (Book p831)

questions.sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831
questions.q: By the 80/20 rule, the adrenal gland is composed of cortex and medulla in the ratio:
questions.exp: The adrenal gland is 80% cortex and 20% medulla. (Book p831)

questions.sec: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rule · p831
questions.q: Within the adrenal medulla, adrenaline and noradrenaline are secreted in the ratio:
questions.exp: The medulla secretes 80% adrenaline and 20% noradrenaline. (Book p831)

questions.sec: Mechanism-based classification and Group I hormones · p832
questions.q: Match the Group I hormone feature — 1) Receptor  2) Solubility  3) Carrier protein  4) t½ … A) Lipophilic  B) Long  C) Intracellular (cytoplasm/nucleus)  D) Present (+)
questions.exp: Group I: intracellular receptor, lipophilic, carrier protein (+), long t½; Group II is the opposite (cell membrane, hydrophilic, −, short). (Book p832)

questions.sec: Mechanism-based classification and Group I hormones · p832
questions.q: Match the Group II hormone feature — 1) Receptor  2) Solubility  3) Carrier protein  4) t½ … A) Hydrophilic  B) Short  C) Cell membrane  D) Absent (−)
questions.exp: Group II: cell-mbrane receptor, hydrophilic, no carrier protein, short t½. (Book p832)

questions.sec: Mechanism-based classification and Group I hormones · p832
questions.q: Group I hormone actions are mediated through the receptor–hormone complex acting mainly on:
questions.exp: Group I acts through gene transcription far more than transport channels. (Book p832)

questions.sec: Mechanism-based classification and Group I hormones · p832
questions.q: Match receptor type to location/hormone — 1) Type I/homodimer  2) Type 2/heterodimer … A) Receptor in nucleus; T3, T4, vitamin A & D  B) Receptor in cytoplasm; steroid hormones
questions.exp: Type I/homodimer receptors sit in the cytoplasm and bind steroid hormones; Type 2/heterodimer receptors sit in the nucleus and bind T3, T4, vitamin A & D. (Book p832)

questions.sec: Mechanism-based classification and Group I hormones · p832
questions.q: In the Type I receptor, the chaperone that holds the receptor in an inactive form is ___.
questions.exp: Hsp-90 is the chaperone keeping the steroid receptor inactive until hormone binds. (Book p832)

questions.sec: Mechanism-based classification and Group I hormones · p832
questions.q: ‘When the steroid hormone binds, Hsp-90 dissociates and the receptor–hormone complex becomes active.’
questions.exp: Hormone binding releases Hsp-90, forming the active R–H complex that enters the nucleus. (Book p832)

questions.sec: Mechanism-based classification and Group I hormones · p832
questions.q: The active steroid receptor–hormone complex binds DNA at the:
questions.exp: The complex binds glucocorticoid response elements (GRE) to drive gene transcription. (Book p832)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: The active form of vitamin D that activates the VDR is ___.
questions.exp: Calcitriol, 1,25(OH)2D3, is the active form of vitamin D that activates the VDR. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: The vitamin D receptor heterodimerizes with which partner before binding DNA?
questions.exp: VDR heterodimerizes with RXR, then the heterodimer binds VDREs to regulate target genes. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: The VDR–RXR heterodimer binds which DNA element?
questions.exp: The heterodimer binds vitamin D response elements (VDREs). (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: ‘The unliganded thyroid receptor is bound to a co-repressor; T3 binding dissociates the co-repressor and recruits a co-activator.’
opts: False — the receptor needs no co-factor
questions.exp: TR is held by CoR until T3 binds, dissociating CoR and recruiting CoA on the TRE to start transcription. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: Which receptor signals as a HOMOdimer rather than a heterodimer?
questions.exp: Steroid receptors are homodimers; TR, VDR, RAR and PPAR are heterodimers. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: Orphan nuclear receptors are characterised by:
opts: No ligands; constitutive activator or repressor binding
questions.exp: Orphan receptors have no ligands and show constitutive activator or repressor binding. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: SF1 and DAX1 (orphan receptors) are required for the development of:
questions.exp: SF1 and DAX1 are required for development of gonadotrophs and the adrenal cortex. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: A defect in HNF4α causes which condition?
questions.exp: HNF4α defect leads to MODY type 1. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: Match the PPAR agonist — 1) PPARα  2) PPARγ  3) Dual PPAR (α & γ) … A) Pioglitazone  B) Clofibrate  C) Saroglitazar
questions.exp: Clofibrate is the PPARα agonist, pioglitazone the PPARγ agonist, saroglitazar the dual agonist. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: PPARα agonists are indicated for hypertriglyceridaemia above:
questions.exp: PPARα agonists treat hypertriglyceridaemia >440 mg/dL (risk of pancreatitis). (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: Pioglitazone (PPARγ) carries risk of:
opts: Salt & water retention, fractures and bladder cancer
questions.exp: PPARγ agonist risks: salt & water retention, fractures, bladder cancer. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: The drug of choice for diabetic dyslipidaemia, NAFLD and NASH is:
questions.exp: Dual PPAR (α & γ) agonist saroglitazar is DOC for diabetic dyslipidaemia, NAFLD and NASH. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Type II receptors, nuclear receptor signalling and PPAR agonists · p833
questions.q: ‘Metformin also combats insulin resistance.’
opts: False — it has no metabolic effect
True, but only in type 1 diabetes
questions.exp: Note: metformin also combats insulin resistance. (Book p833)

questions.sec: Group II hormones: second messengers and GPCR mechanism · p834
questions.q: Group II hormone actions are mediated through:
questions.exp: Group II acts through second messengers affecting transport channels, protein translation, modification and gene transcription. (Book p834)

questions.sec: Group II hormones: second messengers and GPCR mechanism · p834
questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four Group II receptor types listed?
questions.exp: Group II receptor types are GPCR, TKR, JAK/cytokine receptor and STKR; the intracellular steroid receptor is Group I. (Book p834)

questions.sec: Group II hormones: second messengers and GPCR mechanism · p834
questions.q: On hormone binding to a GPCR, the α subunit undergoes which nucleotide change?
opts: GDP converts to GTP and α dissociates to attach to the effector
GTP converts to GDP and α stays bound
ATP converts to cAMP on α
questions.exp: GDP converts to GTP; the α subunit dissociates from the complex and attaches to the effector, activating it. (Book p834)

questions.sec: Group II hormones: second messengers and GPCR mechanism · p834
questions.q: Match G-protein to second messenger — 1) Gs/Gi  2) Gq  3) Gt … A) IP3/DAG  B) cAMP  C) cAMP via transducin
questions.exp: Gs/Gi signal via cAMP, Gq via IP3/DAG, and Gt (transducin) via cAMP. (Book p834)

questions.sec: Group II hormones: second messengers and GPCR mechanism · p834
questions.q: cAMP exerts its effect by converting inactive PKA to active PKA, which then causes:
questions.exp: cAMP activates PKA (protein kinase A) leading to protein phosphorylation and effects. (Book p834)

questions.sec: Group II hormones: second messengers and GPCR mechanism · p834
questions.q: In the Gq pathway, phospholipase C cleaves PIP2 into:
questions.exp: Phospholipase C splits phosphatidylinositol pyrophosphate (PIP2) into DAG and IP3. (Book p834)

questions.sec: Group II hormones: second messengers and GPCR mechanism · p834
questions.q: Match the Gq second messenger to its target — 1) DAG  2) IP3 … A) Activates Ca2+/calmodulin pathway  B) Activates PKC (protein kinase C)
questions.exp: DAG activates PKC; IP3 activates the Ca2+/calmodulin pathway. (Book p834)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: Which hypothalamic hormone signals via cAMP?
questions.exp: Hypothalamus: CRH uses cAMP; TRH and GnRH use IP3/DAG. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: The anterior pituitary hormones that use cAMP are:
questions.exp: Anterior pituitary cAMP hormones: ACTH, FSH, LH, TSH. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: Match vasopressin/oxytocin receptor to messenger — 1) V2  2) V1, V3, oxytocin … A) IP3/DAG  B) cAMP
questions.exp: Posterior pituitary: V2 uses cAMP; V1, V3 and oxytocin use IP3/DAG. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: The vasoconstrictors that signal via IP3/DAG are:
questions.exp: Vasoconstrictors using IP3/DAG: AT II and substance P. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: Match ANS receptor to messenger — 1) α2 (Gi) and β  2) α1 and acetylcholine receptors … A) IP3/DAG  B) cAMP
questions.exp: ANS: α2 (Gi) and β use cAMP; α1 and acetylcholine receptors use IP3/DAG. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: The GIT hormones using cAMP are:
questions.exp: GIT cAMP: secretin, glucagon, somatostatin (Gi); IP3/DAG: CCK, gastrin. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: The miscellaneous hormones signalling via cAMP are:
questions.exp: Miscellaneous cAMP hormones: PTH and calcitonin. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: ‘Gi is inhibitory and lowers cAMP; all other G proteins listed are Gs (stimulatory).’
questions.exp: Gi is inhibitory (↓cAMP); all others are Gs stimulatory. V = vasopressin, AT II = angiotensin II. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: The two cGMP-mediated vasodilators listed are:
opts: Nitric oxide and atrial natriuretic factor (ANF)
questions.exp: cGMP vasodilators: nitric oxide and ANF. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: The most potent vasoconstrictor named is:
questions.exp: Note: urotensin is the most potent vasoconstrictor. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: The TKR mechanism in order is: monomer receptor → ligand →
questions.exp: TKR: ligand causes intracellular dimerisation then receptor autophosphorylation. (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: Insulin signals through the TKR by activating which pathway to mobilise GLUT4?
questions.exp: Insulin activates the PI3K Akt 1/2 pathway, activating GLUT4 (IRS→PI3K→PDK1→Akt). (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: All of the following use TKR EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Growth factors use TKR except TGF β (which uses STKR). (Book p835)

questions.sec: GPCR hormone map, cGMP and TKR · p835
questions.q: GLUT4 mediates insulin-dependent glucose uptake in:
opts: Adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and heart
questions.exp: GLUT4 insulin-dependent uptake occurs in adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and heart. (Book p835)

questions.sec: JAK–STAT and serine–threonine kinase receptors · p836
questions.q: In the JAK–STAT pathway, ligand binding and dimerisation lead to phosphorylation of which protein?
questions.exp: JAK–STAT: ligand binding → dimerisation → phosphorylation of STAT protein → nucleus → transcription. (Book p836)

questions.sec: JAK–STAT and serine–threonine kinase receptors · p836
questions.q: The hormones that use JAK receptors are:
questions.exp: JAK receptors are used by growth hormone, prolactin (twin hormones) and erythropoietin (EPO). (Book p836)

questions.sec: JAK–STAT and serine–threonine kinase receptors · p836
questions.q: Which two hormones are labelled the ‘twin hormones’?
questions.exp: Growth hormone and prolactin are grouped as the twin hormones (both JAK). (Book p836)

questions.sec: JAK–STAT and serine–threonine kinase receptors · p836
questions.q: JAK2 mutations are present in which group of disorders?
opts: Polycythaemia rubra vera, primary myelofibrosis, essential thrombocytosis
questions.exp: JAK2 mutations occur in polycythaemia rubra vera, primary myelofibrosis and essential thrombocytosis. (Book p836)

questions.sec: JAK–STAT and serine–threonine kinase receptors · p836
questions.q: The serine–threonine kinase receptor (STKR) acts by phosphorylating:
questions.exp: STKR signals via phosphorylation of SMAD protein. (Book p836)

questions.sec: JAK–STAT and serine–threonine kinase receptors · p836
questions.q: Hormones using the STKR include:
questions.exp: STKR hormones: activin, inhibin, BMP (bone morphogenetic protein) and TGF-β. (Book p836)

questions.sec: JAK–STAT and serine–threonine kinase receptors · p836
questions.q: The most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine is:
questions.exp: TGF-β is the most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine (TGF: stroke master). (Book p836)

units.title: Structure-based classification of hormones
units.guide: Amino-acid derivatives: tyrosine → T3/T4 and catecholamines (adrenaline 80%, noradrenaline, dopamine); tryptophan → serotonin, melatonin. Vitamin derivatives: A and D. Peptides: small (<50 AA) = ACTH, ADH, oxytocin, all hypothalamic; large (>50 AA) = GH 191, prolactin 199, insulin 51, PTH, renin; glycoproteins (protein > carbohydrate) = FSH/LH/TSH, >200 AA with common α subunit. Steroids: glomerulosa aldosterone, fasciculata cortisol, reticularis DHEAS/androstenedione; sex hormones estrogen/progesterone/testosterone. DHEAS = most abundant adreno-cortical hormone in fetal life.

units.title: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rules
units.guide: Serotonin (enterochromaffin cells of GIT) keeps us alert; melatonin (pineal) aids sleep. Morning light → retinal ganglion cells → raphe nuclei → serotonin; night (9:30–10 pm) serotonin falls and melatonin rises to a 2–2:30 am peak. Night gadget overuse → serotonin stays up → melatonin cannot rise → disrupted sleep–wake → depression. Happiness hormones DOSE. Adrenal 80/20: cortex/medulla; medulla 80% adrenaline/20% noradrenaline.

units.title: Mechanism-based classification and Group I (nuclear) hormones
units.guide: Group I: intracellular receptor, lipophilic, carrier protein (+), long t½; act via gene transcription >> transport channels. Type I/homodimer = cytoplasm, steroids; Type 2/heterodimer = nucleus, T3/T4/vitamin A&D. Steroid receptor held inactive by Hsp-90; hormone binding releases Hsp-90 and the R–H complex binds GREs.

units.title: Type II nuclear receptors, orphan receptors and PPAR agonists
units.guide: VDR (calcitriol = 1,25(OH)2D3) heterodimerizes with RXR and binds VDREs; TR on TRE sheds co-repressor and recruits co-activator on T3 binding. Homodimers = steroid receptors; heterodimers = TR, VDR, RAR, PPAR; orphans (no ligand) = SF1, DAX1 (gonadotrophs + adrenal cortex) and HNF4α (defect → MODY type 1). PPARα clofibrate (TG >440 mg/dL); PPARγ pioglitazone (insulin resistance; risks salt-water retention, fractures, bladder cancer); dual saroglitazar (DOC diabetic dyslipidaemia, NAFLD, NASH). Metformin also combats insulin resistance.

units.title: Group II hormones: second messengers and the GPCR cycle
units.guide: Group II act through second messengers on transport channels, translation, modification and transcription. Receptor types: GPCR, TKR, JAK/cytokine, STKR. GPCR: hormone → GDP→GTP on α, α dissociates to the effector. Gs/Gi → cAMP → PKA → phosphorylation; Gq → PLC on PIP2 → DAG (PKC) + IP3 (Ca2+/calmodulin); Gt = transducin (cAMP).

units.title: The GPCR hormone map, cGMP vasodilators and TKR
units.guide: cAMP users: CRH; ACTH/FSH/LH/TSH; V2; β and α2 (Gi); secretin/glucagon/somatostatin (Gi); PTH/calcitonin. IP3/DAG users: TRH/GnRH; V1/V3/oxytocin; AT II/substance P; α1/ACh; CCK/gastrin. Gi lowers cAMP. cGMP vasodilators: NO and ANF; urotensin = most potent vasoconstrictor. TKR: ligand → dimerisation → autophosphorylation; insulin → PI3K/Akt → GLUT4 (adipose, skeletal muscle, heart); growth factors all use TKR except TGF β.

units.title: JAK–STAT and serine–threonine kinase receptors
units.guide: JAK–STAT: ligand → dimerisation → STAT phosphorylation → transcription; users GH, prolactin (twin hormones), EPO; JAK2 mutations in PRV, primary myelofibrosis, essential thrombocytosis. STKR phosphorylates SMAD; users activin, inhibin, BMP, TGF-β (most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine, 'stroke master').
